symptom: The ElevenLabs sound-effect catalog capped duration_seconds at 22 seconds although the current official endpoint permits up to 30 seconds, making the UI and request contract narrower than the provider contract.
direct_cause: The catalog limit was retained from an older assumption and was not rechecked against the current official request schema before the vendor mapping was inherited.
class_root: Vendor parameter limits were maintained as local constants without a required current-source comparison at the mapping boundary, so a provider expansion could remain hidden behind an unnecessarily narrow control.
affected_population: Users selecting the ElevenLabs sound-effect mapping through the official ElevenLabs vendor catalog.
Future vendor mappings whose local parameter limits are copied without checking the provider's current official contract.
entry_points: ElevenLabs sound-effect duration parameter mapping and validation

external_sources.purpose: Confirms duration_seconds is optional and must be at least 0.5 and at most 30 seconds.

invariants: The ElevenLabs sound-effect duration control accepts values through 30 seconds and rejects values above the official maximum.
The mapping sends the provider's duration_seconds field without silently narrowing a valid official value.
The contract test covers both the official upper bound and the first invalid value.
generality_proof: The correction is anchored at the single ElevenLabs sound-effect mapping and its contract test; the source-backed upper bound is explicit, so later catalog edits can be compared against the same provider field rather than a copied local limit.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the ElevenLabs sound-effect request body and its official duration_seconds parameter mapping.
Expose the provider-backed duration range at the catalog boundary.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The upper bound is 30 seconds and the create mapping uses duration_seconds.
Tests allow exactly 30 seconds and reject 31 seconds.

recurrence.reason: Provider parameter limits can change independently of the local catalog; the same stale-limit class can recur on another ElevenLabs operation or vendor mapping without source-backed checks.
same_class_scan: Compared ElevenLabs sound effects, text-to-speech, music, and speech-to-text catalog fields against the current official API reference pages.
Searched the non-KIE/non-APIMart catalog for adjacent ElevenLabs duration controls and retained only source-backed limits in this correction.

prevention.invariant: Every ElevenLabs sound-effect duration limit is declared once at the mapping boundary and is checked against the current official duration_seconds contract.
prevention.failure_mode: A stale local maximum hides valid provider capacity and causes users to receive a narrower control than the official API supports.
prevention.strategy: Replace the stale 22-second maximum with the official 30-second maximum and pin the boundary with exact upper-bound tests; no parallel fallback is retained.

legacy_paths.rationale: The stale 22-second parameter declaration is removed; the official 30-second declaration is the only active path.
legacy_paths.removal_evidence: The test suite rejects 31 seconds and accepts 30 seconds against the retained mapping.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency is being introduced or retained for this parameter correction.

migration: No persisted data migration is required; the mapping identity and request field remain unchanged.
residual_risks: The official ElevenLabs account key and quota are required for a live audio probe; contract tests do not certify account eligibility or output quality.
